published_statement: NOT READ AT SOURCE. Abstract-level only (web-search summaries, not quotations): [1309.6303] 'solutions of the semiclassical Einstein equation in flat cosmological spacetimes driven by a massive conformally coupled scalar field'; initial conditions at finite time give a state with finite stress-tensor expectation values, controlled by a global estimate; 'existence and uniqueness of local solutions encompassing both the spacetime metric and the matter field simultaneously'; local solutions 'can always be extended up to a point where the scale factor becomes singular or the Hubble function reaches a critical value H_c = 180 pi/G', both a divergence of the scalar curvature. [1001.0864] local (and, per one summary, global) existence in flat cosmological spacetimes coupled to a massive conformally coupled scalar, solving simultaneously for the state and the Hubble function in an integral-functional equation. [2007.14665] existence and uniqueness in flat cosmological spacetimes for a massive scalar with ARBITRARY coupling to R; initial conditions for the scale factor at finite time with a compatible regular state; the highest derivative enters non-locally, standard recursive approximation fails to converge; reformulated as a fixed point of an operator on a Banach space, giving SHORT-TIME existence and uniqueness by the Banach fixed point theorem. [1809.03812] a framework showing existence in cosmological spacetimes WITHOUT restricting to conformal coupling and admitting the full renormalisation freedom, recast as an infinite-dimensional dynamical system with unbounded evolution operators.

lacked_data: These are mathematical existence theorems for a model (flat FLRW + one free massive scalar); no measured datum enters their conclusions (the only constants are the derived anomaly coefficient 1/2880 pi^2 and a symbolic G, C4). So M's hypothesis in its empirical form does not bite here: no later measurement can move them. What the early papers lacked was GENERALITY, not data -- conformal coupling and a restricted renormalisation choice (2011, 2015) were lifted by Gottschalk-Siemssen (full renormalisation freedom, arbitrary xi) and Meda-Pinamonti-Siemssen (arbitrary xi), all at abstract level; global existence remains conditional (1309.6303: up to a or H^2 = 180 pi/G blow-up). For the tree's use none of this matters: the load-bearing field ('m < 0' False) is forced by flat-FLRW geometry itself (C1b) and would survive any data or any generalisation within k = 0; it would NOT survive a move to k = -1 (C1c), which no paper in the row claims.
